findings: FEE DOCTRINE DRIFT (the headline): the fleet charges 30bps/swap in the saos-dex kernel but 20bps/swap in SAOSExchange.sol — two fee doctrines, same fleet. Not a bug today (different venues, no cross-venue flow exists yet) but any future cross-venue router MUST price per venue; the convergence law should pin one doctrine or document the arbitration rule BEFORE the capital path opens (X-2).

MIGRATION LAW: market-grid's 40bps spacing floor is honest ONLY on the chains (internal Hive/Steem markets charge zero trade fee); on the DEX the same grid loses by construction (60bps marginal, 90bps measured at 0.1%-of-depth). The market-grid->DEX bridge must either raise spacing per the measured curve or route maker-only. This kills a whole class of silent-loss migrations before they are coded.

DUST-FLOOR LAW: at dust sizes the DEX's integer-floor semantics dominate cost (400bps on a 0.005%-of-depth round trip; fee floors to zero below ~333 units) — minimum viable DEX rung is depth-scale. The kernel's integers are honest but they price dust OUT of the AMM; dust belongs on the book (maker orders), not in pools.

THE COMPOSITION LAW IS REAL AND NOW MECHANICAL: maker (grid-beat, never crosses) / taker (he_ladder, 97% of bid) / observer (market-grid, paper only) — three layers with zero role overlap, uniform owner-gates, uniform ledger discipline, expiry at the chain cap. The fleet's market stack converges on discipline even where its fee doctrines diverge — the divergence is priced, the discipline is shared.

STATIC-PROXY HONESTY: the 78 function-test surface is a grep count over .t.sol, NOT a forge run — the platform's own CI (foundry-mesh-tests) remains the execution receipt; the desk deliberately does not re-run solidity in the sandbox (the R6-era compile discipline: solc-js harness only when needed, never folded into a desk).
